name: IN-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Jim Baird running with large financial edge
Democratic challenger Drew Cox minimally funded (~$20K raised)
model.rationale: The R+15 district, Baird's incumbency, and his dominant fundraising and outside support leave Cox with no visible path; markets price a Baird win at roughly 94%. With no polls or expert ratings to move the forecast, the fundamentals-based margin stands essentially unchanged.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Baird or a major fundraising turnaround for Cox would be the only realistic signs of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jim Baird seeks another term in a west-central Indiana district that leans Republican by about fifteen points. He enters the general election with a large financial advantage, having raised over $350,000 and drawn more than $500,000 in outside support, while Democrat Drew Cox has raised only about $20,000 and has no outside backing. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give Baird roughly a 94 percent chance of winning.

The forecast rests on the district's partisan lean, Baird's incumbency, and the stark resource gap. A Democratic upset would require an extraordinary, currently unseen shift in the political environment or a late influx of money and attention to Cox's campaign.
